newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria rations water supply in drought-hit towns.
newsitem.headline: Algeria rations water supply in drought-hit towns.

text.p: Drought-stricken Algeria started rationing water supplies on Sunday, limiting millions of people to six hours flow every three days.

The authorities told the nearly three million inhabitants of the capital Algiers and those in nearby Tipaza province they would receive water only for six hours every three days in some districts. Other areas in Algiers would get water for a few hours each day, depending on the network supply.
In other main cities, like western Oran and Constantine in the east, most residents would get some water every day, the authorities said in a statement broadcast on state-run radio.
The government has set up a task force to try to ease the impact of drought on agriculture and industry.

Algeria's state-run media said on Saturday significant rainfall was registered across the country, including in its main crop regions in Chlef, Annaba and Constantine. It said farmers hoped this would save the country's main crops.
Harvesting in southern Algeria usually starts in May and in June in other parts of the country.
